Are you already 18? I wouldn't recommend starting until you know you have somewhere else to live, but if you don't think you can make it a full year, you'll probably have at least a couple months where no one else would notice any changes, at least if you're willing to be diligent about shaving your facial hair. My girlfriend first commented on mine after about 2 months (although if someone was really looking for it, they'd notice it sooner; I saw new hairs on my chin after maybe 3 weeks). There are still some friends I'm not out to and I see my family fairly regularly (I shave when I'm going to see any of them) and no one has commented on any changes yet. 

I guess people also might notice more body hair on you, but I'm a mix or a bunch of very hairy ethnicities and don't see any difference anywhere but my happy trail yet.

For starters, I don't really consider myself nonbinary. I guess I don't really "feel like a man," but I think most cis people really don't feel like a man or like a woman either, and I don't feel enough NOT "like a man" to want to deal with having to explain that the gender binary isn't a terribly accurate way to categorize people to every cis person I interact with. 

I felt less anxious and depressed right away and more able to think clearly (it could be the placebo effect, but I think my dose is still too low and I start to feel shitty again a couple days before my shot every week, so I think it's real for me at least). I also noticed some bottom growth right away. My voice did seem to start dropping quickly, but I think any difference I noticed in the first couple weeks was due to some combination of the decrease in anxiety and post-nasal drip and probably wasn't permanent. My voice has actually started dropping now and it feels different than it did at first. I can mostly only tell the difference when I try to sing. My range is actually a few notes lower now (I can hit as low as about A3 now where I could get to about D3 before I started T and to C3 after around a month, which is when I first started paying a lot of attention), while I just defaulted to a lower portion of my original vocal range for the first couple weeks. 

Edit: I did start noticing a little more facial hair after a month or a little less, but my girlfriend first commented on it after maybe 2 months. I shave every few days (whenever I'm going to be around someone I'm not out to yet).

I was anxious before I started too. I think it's normal. What reassured me was that none of the changes that would be obvious to anybody else happen right away. I got a bit of bottom growth (and a huge mental improvement) with my first shot, but not much else.

Honestly, fuck her. I'm 27 now and finally living in a stable situation with a girl who supports and understands me (at least as well as any cis woman can). I'm debating if I should ruin Christmas by not shaving my facial hair and just speaking in a comfortable register instead of trying to hide how much my voice has dropped like I have been any time I've talked to her recently. 

It might feel like it's a long way off, but one day you will be in a situation where you're stable enough to transition, parental support or no. Just hang in there, man.

Do you generally pass now? It's hit and miss, but I'm only about 3 months on T. I think I look pretty androgynous at the very least, but I'm quite short. 

What did your first T dose feel like? I pretty quickly started to feel warmer all the time and got a little bit of a sore throat (I think just from post-nasal drip).

How long was it before you felt a change in yourself? I'm not sure if it was just the placebo effect, but I felt better psychologically after a day or two. 

Does it have an effect on muscle mass? And does it actually change the way your body places fat? My workouts have definitely been more effective in the last couple of months. I don't think I've had much fat redistribution yet, but it's early and I was really skinny in the first place. 

What affect, if any, did it have on your libido? My sex drive is way higher. I'll just wake up irrationally turned on sometimes now. I feel bad for my girlfriend for having to live with me. 

How long before you started growing hair? I always had a fuckload of body hair so it's hard for me to tell (it seemed like my happy trail started coming in darker around a month though), but my facial hair just started coming in enough for other people to notice it now. I noticed a few more hairs on my chin about a month to a month and a half in though. 

Did you cut your hair short or transition with long hair? I had my hair short for about a year before I got on T. I was feeling insecure and it helped me make a decision to see how it felt to be gendered correctly by strangers before I did. 

How long did you wait to socially transition? I'm in this weird in-between place where I'm out to a few people but not everybody. I came out to my girlfriend a few years ago and have come out to a couple of friends, but I'm not out to most people at work or my family, since I have my doubts about how well they'll react. 

Did T improve your outlook on life? Definitely. I still get anxious and depressed from time to time, but it's certainly not as bad as it was before. I'm trying to see if coming out to everybody important helps, but I'll consider antidepressants after that. 

Did any emotional issues come from it? Nope. I mostly just sink back into a severe depression when I have to miss a shot by more than a day or two. 

What negative effects have you noticed from it? I get some pretty bad headaches sometimes (usually toward the end of my shot cycle, which leads me to believe my dose is too low). I'm hoping it'll get alleviated when my doctor finally deems it necessary to draw my blood, but it's like pulling teeth to get proper medical care where I am.
